Cross-Fitted Non-Linear Calibration for Prediction-Powered Inference

Source: R/ppi_calibrated.R
ppi_calibrated.Rd

Handles non-linear LLM scoring distortions (ceiling/floor compression, S-curve saturation, quadratic distortion, or covariate-specific non-linear bias) by learning a flexible calibration mapping \(\hat{m}(\hat{Y}, X) \approx Y\) via strict \(K\)-fold cross-fitting on the human-validated subset before applying Prediction-Powered Inference (PPI++). Because every labeled observation's calibrated score is computed strictly out-of-fold and unlabeled observations average the \(K\) fold-specific calibrators with exact fold-size weights, the canonical-link PPI++ rectifier preserves exact unbiasedness and nominal 95% CI coverage while dramatically reducing standard errors relative to both Human-Only and uncalibrated linear PPI++.

Usage

ppi_calibrated(
  formula,
  data,
  pred_col,
  family = stats::gaussian(),
  unlabeled = NULL,
  calibrator = c("spline", "poly", "logistic"),
  df = 4L,
  folds = 5L,
  include_covariates = TRUE,
  lambda = "auto",
  conf_level = 0.95,
  seed = 1234L
)

Arguments

formula

Two-sided model formula (e.g., human_y ~ x1 + x2 or human_y ~ 1 for calibrated mean estimation).

data

A data.frame containing response, predictors, and pred_col. When unlabeled = NULL, rows with missing response form the unlabeled set.

pred_col

Name of the numeric LLM prediction column to calibrate.

family

Canonical GLM family: gaussian() (default), binomial(), or poisson().

unlabeled

Optional separate data.frame of unlabeled observations.

calibrator

Non-linear calibration learner:

  • "spline" (default): natural cubic spline (splines::ns()) on pred_col plus optional covariates from formula.

  • "poly": polynomial basis of degree df on pred_col plus covariates.

  • "logistic": binomial GLM with natural cubic spline on pred_col plus covariates (ideal for binary outcomes).

  • Or a custom function function(train_df, new_df, truth_col, pred_col, rhs_vars) returning numeric calibrated predictions for new_df.

df

Positive integer basis degrees of freedom (for "spline" / "logistic") or polynomial degree (for "poly"). Default 4L.

folds

Integer number of cross-fitting folds (>= 2L). Default 5L.

include_covariates

Logical; if TRUE (default), includes main effects of RHS predictors from formula inside the calibration model so covariate-specific bias (DPF) is removed before PPI++.

lambda

Power-tuning parameter passed to PPI++: "auto" (default) or numeric scalar in [0, 1].

conf_level

Confidence level in (0, 1). Default 0.95.

seed

Integer random seed for deterministic fold assignment (preserves global .Random.seed). Default 1234L.

Value

An S3 object of class c("llm_ppi_calibrated", "llm_ppi") containing all standard llm_ppi components (with $benchmarks comparing ppi++_calibrated, ppi++_uncalibrated, human_only, and naive_llm) plus $calibration_diagnostics (r_raw, r_calibrated_oof, rmse_raw, rmse_calibrated_oof, folds, calibrator).

Examples

set.seed(42)
n_tot <- 800
x <- rnorm(n_tot)
y_true <- 1.0 + 1.2 * x + rnorm(n_tot, sd = 0.8)
# Severely non-linear S-curve compressed LLM scores
y_llm <- 5 * plogis(1.4 * (y_true - 1.0) + 0.5 * x) + rnorm(n_tot, sd = 0.15)
df <- tibble::tibble(
  x = x,
  human_y = c(y_true[1:140], rep(NA_real_, n_tot - 140)),
  llm_y = y_llm
)
fit <- ppi_calibrated(human_y ~ x, data = df, pred_col = "llm_y")
fit
#> 
#> ── Prediction-Powered Inference (ppi++_calibrated) 
#> Labeled n = 140 | Unlabeled N = 660 | lambda = 0.674 | CI = 95%
#> Cross-fitted calibration (spline, 5-fold, df=4): r 0.940 -> 0.957 | RMSE 1.634
#> -> 0.443
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   term        estimate std_error conf_low conf_high p_value var_gain
#>   <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>      <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)    0.982    0.0466    0.890      1.07 <0.0001     2.29
#> 2 x              1.27     0.065     1.14       1.39 <0.0001     1.07
